translation_notes: The bound variable `typedObject` is NOT projected by the query (SELECT ?typeAssertion WHERE {...}); per INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS4 that is the case for a bare interpolation in term position, so `initBindings={'typedObject': typed_object}` becomes `{typed_object}` written directly where `?typedObject` stood.

`_TYPE_QUERY = prepareQuery("""...""")` was a module-level prepared-query object passed to `g.query(_TYPE_QUERY, ...)`; `s{ }` requires its query text literal at the island site, so that variable and the `prepareQuery` call collapse into the island written directly inside `get_type_assertions`. ldpy prepares and caches queries itself (a small hand-written LRU, querying.md) so nothing is lost by not naming the prepared query -- it moved from a Python-level cache to the transpiler's own.

The query never declares `PREFIX rdf:` and the original code never passes `initNs` either: it relies on rdflib's implicit default namespace bindings (a fresh Graph() binds rdf/rdfs/xsd/xml automatically), which `Graph.query()` falls back to when no PREFIX/initNs is given. `s{ }` does NOT inherit that fallback -- its prologue comes only from `@prefix` declarations lexically in scope (traced in ldpy/runtime.py: `PreparedQuery._execute` calls `graph.query(prep, ...)` with `prep` already compiled by `prepareQuery(text, initNs=dict(namespaces))`, `namespaces` being exactly the @prefix set at the island, nothing more). So `@prefix rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .` had to be added explicitly, even though the original source never wrote it: a fidelity trap worth flagging for the study, since it is invisible in a diff against the query TEXT alone.

added `from rdflib.plugins.sparql import prepareQuery` to original.py only, to restore the top-of-file import the real repo has (see original.py) -- not needed on the ldpy side since s{ } prepares its own query.

Rewritten from s{ } to m{ } (2026-11-02, PI decision): the query is a pure basic graph pattern with one projected variable, SELECT without DISTINCT (a graph holds each triple once, so each ?typeAssertion yields one solution under both forms). `{typed_object}` is interpolated in object position; with one projected variable m{ } yields bare terms, so `[x for (x,) in query_result]` becomes `list(type_assertions)`.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `query_result` is inlined, which gives `return [x for (x,) in g.query(_TYPE_QUERY, initBindings=...)]`. The module-level prepared query `_TYPE_QUERY` stays. Moving its text into the call would save two names, but rdflib would then parse the query on every call, and the author prepared it once on purpose.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `return list(m{ ?typeAssertion a rdf:Statement ; rdf:predicate rdf:type ; rdf:subject {typed_object} }(g))`. The three patterns share their subject (`;`), and translated.ldpy's intermediate `type_assertions` goes. `_TYPE_QUERY` and its prepareQuery have no counterpart, because m{ } replaces the whole query. These are RDF lines, so this is not an exception to the symmetry rule.
header_optimization_notes: Nothing unused in either header. The Python header imports prepareQuery, which `_TYPE_QUERY` uses. The ldpy header declares only `@prefix rdf:`, which the pattern uses. The two files are copies of the optimized ones.
